The *Pañcaputtakhādapetivatthu* (Pv 6) is a canonical verse text belonging to the *Petavatthu* collection in the Pali Sutta Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Translated by Bhikkhu Sujato as "Eater of Five Sons", the narrative features a female ghost (*petī*) who describes her intense torment, recounting how her present misery arose directly from lying and evil deeds committed during a former human existence [SuttaCentral]. Five modern translations across five languages are indexed on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

In terms of textual reuse, the verses of the text are heavily preserved and commented upon in the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, which accounts for 69 shared text segments according to computational analyses [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, the text shares extensive formulaic and thematic verse passages with several other *Petavatthu* narratives [DharmaNexus]. It shares its largest match with the contiguous *Sattaputtakhādapetivatthu* (Pv 7, segments 0.1–5.4), alongside recurring verse passages found in the *Seriṇīpetivatthu* (Pv 31), the *Mattāpetivatthu* (Pv 15), and the *Saṁsāramocakapetivatthu* (Pv 13) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus further aligns segment 5.3 of the text with Tibetan narrative materials, including Kṣemendra's *Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā* (D4155-2) and Kangyur text BO_K10_D0343_H0351 [DharmaNexus].
